I write such applications. (Not the ones you mentioned specifically).

The answer is, it depends.

The architecture of the system is going to depend on the purpose of the program. In my system a node can function both as a master and a slave. Masters broadcast "problems" that need to be "solved" to connected peers (slaves). Those slaves in turn either work on the problem, and / or become a master to other slaves delegating the problem to other nodes. Lather, rinse, repeat, until you have thousands of nodes solving the problem.

When a solution is found, the slave sends it's solution to it's master. If that master was a slave it also pushes again until the originating master receives that answer.

This is a simplistic answer. It's much more complicated than just this. But this describes the most important aspects.
